newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seen starting lower on U.S. worries.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seen starting lower on U.S. worries.

text.p: French shares were expected to decline at the opening, reflecting weaker bonds and losses on Wall Street overnight. Concerns over a possible rise in U.S. interest rates fuelled caution among investors, following yesterday's Beige Book report on the American economy.
U.S. retail sales data are due today at 1330 GMT, with the market looking for 0.6 percent rise in February. Producer prices statistics appear tomorrow.
At 0830 GMT, the CAC-40 futures contract on GLOBEX was down 22.5 at 2,634 from Wednesday's close. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 44.45 points or 1.65 percent at 2,641 on Wednesday.
* Cap Gemini to pay 1996 net dividend of two francs after several years of non-payment.

* Axa-UAP chairman says in newspaper La Tribune the insurer is not interested in buying GAN, or selling U.S. DLJ investment bank. He prefers a link-up between British Sun Life and Equity and Law rather than disposals.
